summary: The handoff workflow and the store operations are clear, but persisted review notes have no format and no portable subject identity, which is the biggest gap for sharing notes between Web, MCP and the archive.

questions.text: How is a note's subject (CapturedWork or EvaluatedResult) identified durably once the note is persisted and archived?
questions.reason: Archived notes keep their subjects, but captures are never saved and candidate directories are local; 0023 'EvaluatedResult retains exact result identity' vs 0010 'Store-local locations are not committed as portable identities in the archive'.

questions.text: What is the on-disk format of a review note under notes/, including file naming, ReviewNoteId generation and how subject and target are encoded?
questions.reason: Notes are committed in the archive and shared by Web and MCP processes, so the format is a data-compatibility choice; 0010 only says '`notes/` review notes, excluded from evaluation inputs'.

questions.text: What are ExampleId, ArtifactId and SourceSpan: the example name, a point or a range, and which store owns artifacts?
questions.reason: Examples are keyed by name (0006 'Metadata retains the original name and it must match the directory'), 0011 has 'SourceLocation file line column' as a point, and 0017 names ArtifactId without defining its store.

questions.text: What 'revision checks' guard concurrent note, example and Ready/Draft writes from separate Web and MCP processes?
questions.reason: Whether writes carry an expected capture or candidate identity changes the operation signatures; 0023 'support multiple clients with revision checks' vs 0012 'Simultaneous edits of an uncommitted workspace are also their responsibility'.

questions.text: How do addReviewNote and saveExample report domain refusals such as a target not meaningful in its subject, when they return no Either?
questions.reason: 0023 requires 'Targets must be meaningful within their subject' and 0011's encodeExample returns Either [Diagnostic], but both 0023 signatures only have Failure, which 0019 reserves for operational failures.

questions.text: Which outputs or queries, with which arguments, are evaluated on Before and the candidate to produce 'selected view-output differences', and are the results saved?
questions.reason: This decides whether review needs RootExecution on both endpoints, stored comparison arguments, and persisted artifacts for ArtifactTarget notes; 0023 only lists 'selected view-output differences' as a dimension.

questions.text: Can review notes be resolved, edited or deleted, and through which operations; do they record an author and time?
questions.reason: The handoff loop needs to show which notes are outstanding, but only addReviewNote is defined; 0010 export accepts 'additions and deletions' in notes/ without defining an operation.

questions.text: Does saveExample replace or refuse an existing example with the same name?
questions.reason: Editing an expectation from a Web form needs replacement, accidental overwrite argues for refusal; 0023 says saving 'writes target/examples/' and marks the workspace Draft, nothing on collisions.

questions.text: ADR 0023 makes recordHistory an EvolutionStore operation that reads Git, but ADR 0010's runEvolutionStore interpreter has no Git dependency.
questions.reason: Either every EvolutionStore composition gains Git or history needs its own capability; 0023 'The initial implementation reads Git and archived reports directly' vs 0010 'runEvolutionStore :: (RootStore, WorkspaceStore, FileSystem, DhallHandling, Failure)'.

questions.text: How does recordHistory's flat [RecordHistoryEntry] result represent Git parent links across merges?
questions.reason: 0023 requires 'preserve Git parent links when presenting merges', but RecordHistoryEntry has no parent field, so the return type or traversal must change.
